# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1156

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃1156화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스켈레톤 킹이 척 헤이글과의 대화에서 무언가를 떠올린 그때, 그들의 대화 속 주인공은 최고의 보안을 갖춘 펜타곤(Pentagon)에서도 가장 깊고 비밀스러운 공간에 홀로 서 있었다.
  6|
  7|아니, 어쩌면 홀로 서 있다는 표현에는 약간의 어폐가 있을지도 몰랐다.
  8|
  9|엄밀히 말한다면, 그는 ‘혼자’가 아니었으므로.
 10|
 11|“자주 찾아뵀어야 했는데, 사정이 있어서 좀 늦었습니다.”
 12|
 13|문득 입을 연 진태경은 주위를 천천히 둘러보았다. 수백 개의 조명을 켜 놓은 듯이 환하고, 공허하게 느껴질 만큼 드넓은 백색 공간을.
 14|
 15|“얼마 전에 이사하셨다는 얘기는 들었습니다. 이런 곳일 줄은 몰랐지만요.”
 16|
 17|그래. 정말 몰랐다. 그래서 이곳에 처음 발을 디딘 순간 놀랄 수밖에 없었다.
 18|
 19|그만큼 닮아 있었으니까.
 20|
 21|그가 인벤토리(Inventory)라고 부르는, 얼마 전 생각지도 못한 만남이 있었던 그 미지의 공간과.
 22|
 23|“단순한 우연의 일치겠죠. 아마도.”
 24|
 25|틀림없이 그럴 것이다. 오직 한 사람을 위해 심혈을 기울여 이 비밀 공간을 설계한 거구의 대마도사는, 인벤토리의 형태는커녕 그 존재조차 모르고 있을 테니.
 26|
 27|하지만…….
 28|
 29|“솔직히 이제는 아무것도 모르겠습니다. 제가 정확히 어떤 것을 알고 있는지, 무엇이 진실이고 거짓인지조차도요.”
 30|
 31|어느 날인가부터 모든 상식이 파괴되기 시작했다. 불가해(不可解)와 맞닿은 현실 앞에서 이성은 흐려졌고, 그 빈자리를 직감이 채웠다.
 32|
 33|진태경 그 자신조차도 쉽게 이해할 수 없는, 어설픈 공상에 가까운 직감이.
 34|
 35|그리고 이 모든 것의 시작이자 끝이라 할 수 있는 존재가 지금 이 순간 그의 망막에 비치고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“듣고 있습니까. 보고 있습니까.”
 38|
 39|진태경은 고개를 숙여 내려다보았다.
 40|
 41|온갖 마법진과 기계 장치로 연결된 타원형의 회복 캡슐을.
 42|
 43|살아 있는 자를 위해 마련된 관(棺)과 같은 그곳에서, 누구도 깨울 수 없는 깊은 잠에 빠진 한 노인을.
 44|
 45|“그렇다면, 대답해 주십시오.”
 46|
 47|물론 진태경은 알고 있었다. 아무리 오랫동안 묻고 또 기다려도 돌아오는 대답은 없으리라는 것을.
 48|
 49|하지만 그럼에도, 물어봐야만 했다.
 50|
 51|“당신이, 제가 짐작하는 그 사람이 맞습니까?”
 52|
 53|인류가 낳은 가장 위대한 영웅.
 54|
 55|본명은 천태민, 이명은 슬레이어(Slayer) 혹은 스카이(Sky).
 56|
 57|그리고.
 58|
 59|“무신(武神).”
 60|
 61|진태경은 참았던 숨을 토해 냈다.
 62|
 63|뜨거운 숨결에 닿아 수증기가 낀 반투명한 막 너머로, 평온하게 잠든 천태민의 얼굴을 응시했다.
 64|
 65|“나는 느낄 수 있었습니다. 그때 그곳에서 만난 사람은…… 당신이었습니다. 분명히.”
 66|
 67|칙. 치지직!
 68|
 69|어느덧 한층 높아진 목소리가 공간을 울리고, 자연스럽게 힘이 들어간 손이 캡슐을 둘러싼 무수한 방어 마법과 충돌한다. 그러나 피부로 전해지는 통증에도 진태경은 개의치 않았다.
 70|
 71|그는 얼마 전에야 떠올린 반쪽짜리 확신에 대한 답을 들어야 했다.
 72|
 73|눈앞의 천태민과 도우미 노인이 같은 사람이라는 것을 확인해야 했고, 그 역시 자신과 같은 플레이어(Player)였다는 사실을 알아야 했으며 어찌하여 지금의 상황에 이르렀는지.
 74|
 75|그리고 무엇보다.
 76|
 77|“왜, 왜 깨어나지 않는 겁니까.”
 78|
 79|아무리 억누르고 또 억눌러도, 계속해서 들끓어 오르는 가슴 속 분노를 토해 낼 곳이 필요했다.
 80|
 81|“……도대체 어째서.”
 82|
 83|당신에 비하면 턱없이 부족한 내가, 이런 무거운 짐을 감당해야 하는 겁니까.
 84|
 85|그 순간.
 86|
 87|치익.
 88|
 89|차마 끝까지 내뱉지 못한 목소리와 함께, 진태경은 캡슐에서 손을 뗐다.
 90|
 91|그리고 돌아서며 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 92|
 93|“뭐야, 면회 인원은 한 번에 한 명만 되는 거 아니었어요?”
 94|
 95|앞서 말을 멈춘 것은, 비단 통제할 수 없을 정도로 출렁이던 감정 때문만이 아니다.
 96|
 97|조금 전 도착한 두 번째 면회객이 대답했다.
 98|
 99|“글쎄요, 제가 알기론 그런 규정은 없습니다. 설령 있다 하더라도 가족은 예외로 둬야죠.”
100|
101|“와, 그렇게 말씀하시니까 뭐라 할 말이 없네.”
102|
103|“참고로 말씀드리자면, 전 지금 막 왔습니다.”
104|
105|“도둑이 제 발 저린다더니, 누가 뭐래요?”
106|
107|앞서 보인 모습이 무색할 만큼, 평소와 다를 것 없이 장난기가 묻어 나오는 표정과 어조.
108|
109|그런 진태경을 물끄러미 바라보던 최 팀장, 최민우가 이내 어깨를 으쓱하며 말을 받았다.
110|
111|“노크라도 할 걸 그랬군요. 어차피 결계 마법이라 아무런 소리도 안 나겠지만.”
112|
113|“뭐 그럴 것까지야.”
114|
115|“갑자기 외조부님 생각이 나서 미스터 존슨을 찾았더니, 이미 진태경 씨와 함께 가셨다는 얘길 들었습니다. 실례가 됐다면 미안합니다.”
116|
117|“실례는 무슨, 이 경우는 오히려 내가 방해한 거지.”
118|
119|웃으며 손을 내저은 진태경이 걸음을 뗀 그때였다.
120|
121|“혹시, 어떤 이유로 외조부님을 찾아뵈러 온 건지 물어봐도 되겠습니까?”
122|
123|잠시 침묵하던 진태경이 피식 웃었다.
124|
125|“왜요, 우려할 만한 상황이라도 일어날까 봐?”
126|
127|지금 같은 상황에서 우려할 만한 상황이라면 한 가지뿐이다.
128|
129|바로 진태경이 천태민과 함께 단둘이 드래곤 레어로 향하는 것.
130|
131|물론 천태민은 이미 오래전부터 의식불명 상태였고, 그런 상황은 펜타곤의 그 누구도 원하지 않으니 이와 같은 일이 벌어진다면 그것은 사실상 진태경의 독단에 의한 것일 터였다.
132|
133|하지만 농담처럼 던진 진태경의 물음과 달리, 곧이어 돌아온 최민우의 목소리는 낮게 가라앉아 있었다.
134|
135|“네.”
136|
137|“……!”
138|
139|“솔직히 말씀드리자면, 매우 우려되는군요.”
140|
141|눈을 크게 뜬 진태경이 뭐라 대꾸하기도 전에, 최민우가 담담하게 덧붙였다.
142|
143|“당신이, 진태경 씨가 홀로 모르고스와 맞서 싸우려는 멍청한 선택을 할까 봐 우려됩니다.”
144|
145|“…….”
146|
147|“대답해 주십시오. 부정하고 싶으면 그래도 됩니다.”
148|
149|최민우를 말없이 응시하던 진태경이 입을 열었다.
150|
151|“좋아요. 이 기회에 확실하게 말하자면, 절대 그럴 일 없어요.”
152|
153|“그렇군요.”
154|
155|“예. 그럼 이걸로 된 거죠?”
156|
157|“아뇨.”
158|
159|“아니, 왜?”
160|
161|“그 말을 전혀 믿지 못하겠으니까요.”
162|
163|“……!”
164|
165|“진태경 씨를 잘 아는 사람이라면 누구나 그럴 겁니다. 곁에서 지켜보면 자연스럽게 깨닫게 되거든요. 당신이 얼마나 무모하고 바보 같은 선택을 하는지.”
166|
167|가까이 다가온 최민우가 회복 캡슐 안에 잠들어 있는 외조부를 바라보며 말을 이었다.
168|
169|“제 외할아버지도 그런 분이셨겠죠. 그만큼 두 분은 서로를 닮았으니까.”
170|
171|“닮았다고요?”
172|
173|“예. 그 덕분에 조금은 개인적인 위안을 얻기도 했습니다. 그것도 아주 최근에요.”
174|
175|“그게 무슨…….”
176|
177|“진태경 씨는 중동에서 돌아오신 이후에도 가족분들을 찾지 않으시더군요. 바로 이곳 펜타곤에 머무르고 계시는데도 말입니다.”
178|
179|가족.
180|
181|그 짧은 한 단어에 진태경의 눈동자가 파르르 떨렸다.
182|
183|맞다. 어머니와 여동생. 그에게 있어 세상 그 무엇보다 소중한, 피로 이어진 가족들은 이미 한참 전부터 펜타곤에서 보호받고 있다.
184|
185|하지만 단 한 번도 찾지 않았다.
186|
187|아니, 만나서는 안 되었다.
188|
189|만약 그들을 만난다면, 자신을 가까스로 지탱하고 있는 보이지 않는 기둥이 무너져 버릴 테니까.
190|
191|이대로 허물어져 버린다면, 정말 한 줌의 용기조차 쥐어 짜내지 못할 테니까.
192|
193|“다른 길드원들과의 만남을 거부하시는 것도, 분명 그런 이유일 테고요.”
194|
195|그간 수많은 헌터와 인연을 맺어 왔지만, 진태경과 최민우에게 있어 길드원이라 부를 수 있는 사람은 이제 둘뿐이다.
196|
197|송송이와 임꺽정.
198|
199|그리고 진태경은 그들과의 만남도 회피했다.
200|
201|그가 걸어가야 하는 길은 무수한 위험이 도사린 사지(死地).
202|
203|죽음은 모두에게 공평하나, 죽음이 찾아오는 속도는 그렇지 않다.
204|
205|그렇다면 S급 헌터도, 초절정 고수도 아닌 그들이 곧 벌어질 대전투에 참여한다면 어떻게 될까.
206|
207|‘죽겠지. 분명히.’
208|
209|이건 비단 진태경 자신만이 아닌, 수십억 인류의 목숨이 판돈으로 걸린 거대한 도박판이다.
210|
211|삼성(三星)도, 화왕(火王)도 없는 이 세상에서 오직 홀로 짊어져야 하는 그 막중한 무게를 그는 감당할 수 없었다.
212|
213|그래서 도망쳤다.
214|
215|가족들에게서, 친구들에게서.
216|
217|주위의 모두에게서 도망쳐 이곳으로 왔다.
218|
219|이런 자신을 이해할 수 있는 유일한 사람. 모든 것의 해답이자 열쇠가 될 수 있는 천태민을 이렇게라도 다시 한번 마주하고 싶어서.
220|
221|그리고 다음 순간 귓가로 흘러들어오는 최민우의 음성에, 진태경은 불현듯 깨달았다.
222|
223|“그런 진태경 씨의 모습을 보고 있자니, 그제야 문득 알 것 같았습니다. 하나뿐인 손주를 찾지 않았던 외할아버지의 마음을.”
224|
225|지금까지 미처 알아차리지 못했던 한 가지 사실을.
226|
227|“어떻게든 이유를 찾고 싶은 저만의 바램일지도 모릅니다만…… 이제는 그렇게 생각하려고 합니다. 그분만이 느끼고 계셨을 어떠한 위험 때문에 애써 저를 멀리하실 수밖에 없었다고요.”
228|
229|저 쓴웃음 섞인 목소리에 담긴, 최민우조차도 알아차리지 못한 진짜 의미를.
230|
231|‘오직 그만이 느끼고 있었을 위험, 이라고?’
232|
233|그럴 리 없다. 당시의 인류에게 더 이상의 위험은 존재하지 않았으니까.
234|
235|그토록 강대하던 마왕 아스모데우스는 육신조차 남기지 못한 채 가루가 되어 소멸했고, 오대양 육대주를 피로 물들이던 몬스터 군단 역시 한낱 사냥감으로 전락한 상황.
236|
237|하지만 어째서인지 이 위대한 업적을 이루어 낸 영웅은, 평화가 찾아옴과 동시에 스스로를 세상과 격리시켰다.
238|
239|그는 모두를 멀리했다.
240|
241|그 누구도 예외는 없었다.
242|
243|의형제나 다름없던 최측근들도, 세상 그 무엇보다 소중하게 여겼다는 딸도.
244|
245|심지어 그 딸이 불의의 사고로 인해 남편과 함께 세상을 떠났을 때도, 어린 외손자를 가까이에서 돌보는 대신 김 집사에게 맡겼다.
246|
247|그리고 어느 날, 아무런 예고도 없이 의식을 잃었다.
248|
249|그것도 무려 십수 년 동안이나.
250|
251|‘……당신도 그만큼 두려웠던 겁니까.’
252|
253|혀끝에서 삼켜 낸 한마디와 함께, 진태경은 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 천태민을 바라보았다.
254|
255|자신이 옳았다.
256|
257|여전히 확실한 증거도, 증언도 없었지만 방금 최민우가 한 말을 통해 다시금 깨닫게 되었다.
258|
259|천태민과 무신은 처음부터 동일 인물이었다는 것을.
260|

[P22]

[P23]
“Are you the person I think you are?”

[P24]
The greatest hero humanity had ever produced.

[P25]
His real name was Cheon Taemin. His titles were Slayer and Sky.

[P26]
And…

[P27]
“The Martial God.”

[P28]
Jin Taekyung let out the breath he’d been holding.

[P29]

[P30]
“I could feel it. The person I met back then, in that place… was you. I’m sure of it.”

[P31]
Hiss. Crackle!

[P32]

[P33]
He needed an answer to the conviction he’d only recently arrived at, incomplete though it was.

[P34]
He needed to confirm that Cheon Taemin and the old man he called The Helper were the same person. That Cheon Taemin, too, had been a Player like him. And he needed to know how things had come to this.

[P35]
More than anything—

[P36]
“Why? Why won’t you wake up?”

[P37]
No matter how hard he tried to hold it back, the anger in his chest kept boiling over. He needed somewhere to let it out.

[P38]
“…Why?”

[P39]
*Why do I, who fall so far short of you, have to bear this burden?*

[P40]
At that moment—

[P41]
Hiss.

[P42]
Unable to speak the thought aloud, Jin Taekyung pulled his hand from the capsule.

[P43]
Then he turned and blurted, “What, I thought it was one visitor at a time?”

[P44]
His surging emotions weren’t the only reason he’d stopped speaking. A second visitor had just arrived.

[P45]
“As far as I know, there’s no such rule. And even if there were, family ought to be an exception.”

[P46]
“Wow. When you put it like that, what can I say?”

[P47]
“For the record, I only just got here.”

[P48]
“Guilty conscience? I didn’t accuse you of anything.”

[P49]
Jin Taekyung’s expression and tone were as playful as ever, at odds with how he’d been only moments before.

[P50]
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—watched him for a moment, then shrugged.

[P51]
“I should have knocked. Not that it would have made a sound through the barrier magic.”

[P52]
“You didn’t have to go that far.”

[P53]
“I suddenly thought of my grandfather and went looking for Mr. Johnson. I heard he’d already brought you here. I’m sorry if I intruded.”

[P54]
“Don’t be. If anything, I’m the one intruding.”

[P55]
Jin Taekyung smiled and waved a hand as he started walking.

[P56]
“May I ask why you came to see my grandfather?”

[P57]
After a moment’s silence, Jin Taekyung gave a short laugh.

[P58]
“What, worried something might happen?”

[P59]
In a situation like this, there was only one thing to worry about: Jin Taekyung taking Cheon Taemin to the Dragon Lair, just the two of them.

[P60]
Cheon Taemin had been unconscious for years, and no one in the Pentagon wanted that to happen. If it did, Jin Taekyung would effectively have acted on his own.

[P61]
But while Jin Taekyung’s question had sounded like a joke, Choi Minwoo’s answer came in a low, steady voice.

[P62]
“Yes.”

[P63]
“…!”

[P64]
“To be honest, I’m very worried.”

[P65]
Before Jin Taekyung could respond, Choi Minwoo added calmly, “I’m worried you’ll make the stupid choice to fight Morgoth alone.”

[P66]
“…”

[P67]
“Answer me, please. Deny it if you want.”

[P68]
Jin Taekyung stared at him in silence, then spoke.

[P69]
“Fine. Let me make this perfectly clear. I would never do that.”

[P70]
“I see.”

[P71]
“Yeah. So that settles it, right?”

[P72]
“No.”

[P73]
“What? Why not?”

[P74]
“Because I don’t believe you at all.”

[P75]
“…!”

[P76]
“Anyone who knows you well would feel the same. Spend enough time around you, and you see how often you make reckless, foolish choices.”

[P77]

[P78]
“My grandfather must have been the same way. The two of you are so alike.”

[P79]
“Alike?”

[P80]
“Yes. Realizing that has brought me a little comfort. Only very recently, in fact.”

[P81]
“What do you mean…?”

[P82]
“Even after you returned from the Middle East, you haven’t gone to see your family. Though they’re right here in the Pentagon, where you’ve been staying.”

[P83]
*Family.*

[P84]

[P85]
His mother and younger sister. His family by blood, more precious to him than anything else in the world, had been under the Pentagon’s protection for quite some time.

[P86]
But he hadn’t gone to see them once.

[P87]
No. He couldn’t see them.

[P88]
If he did, the invisible pillar barely holding him up would collapse. And if he crumbled now, he wouldn’t be able to summon even the smallest shred of courage.

[P89]
“You’ve refused to meet the other Guild members, too. I’m sure it’s for the same reason.”

[P90]
Jin Taekyung had come to know countless Hunters, but there were only two people left whom he and Choi Minwoo could call Guild members.

[P91]
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong.

[P92]
Jin Taekyung had avoided them, too.

[P93]
The path ahead of him was riddled with danger. Death came for everyone, but it didn’t come for everyone at the same speed.

[P94]
What would happen if those two joined the battle to come, when neither was an S-rank Hunter or a Supreme Peak master?

[P95]
*They’d die. Without a doubt.*

[P96]
This was a colossal gamble with the lives of billions at stake, not just his own. In a world without the Three Saints or the Fire King, he couldn’t bear the weight he alone had to carry.

[P97]
So he ran.

[P98]
From his family. From his friends.

[P99]
He’d fled everyone around him and come here, wanting to face Cheon Taemin once more, even like this. The only person who could understand him. The person who might hold the answer—and the key—to everything.

[P100]
Then Choi Minwoo’s next words reached him, and Jin Taekyung realized something.

[P101]
“Watching you, Mr. Jin, I think I finally understand why my grandfather never came to see his only grandson.”

[P102]
Something he’d failed to notice until now.

[P103]
“Maybe I just want to find a reason for it. But… I’ve decided to think that he had no choice but to keep me at a distance because of some danger only he could sense.”

[P104]
Choi Minwoo’s voice held a bitter smile. And in his words was a meaning even he hadn’t noticed.

[P105]
*Some danger only he could sense?*

[P106]
That couldn’t be. At the time, there had been no danger left for humanity.

[P107]
The once-mighty Demon King Asmodeus had been reduced to dust, without even a body left behind. The monster legions that had stained the Five Oceans and Six Continents with blood had become nothing more than prey.

[P108]
Yet as soon as peace arrived, the hero who had achieved that great feat shut himself away from the world.

[P109]
He kept everyone at a distance.

[P110]
No one was an exception.

[P111]
Not his closest companions, who were practically sworn brothers. Not even the daughter he was said to have cherished more than anything.

[P112]
When that daughter and her husband died in an accident, he left his young grandson in Butler Kim’s care rather than look after the boy himself.

[P113]
Then, one day, without warning, he lost consciousness.

[P114]
And remained unconscious for more than a decade.

[P115]
*…Were you that afraid, too?*

[P116]
Jin Taekyung swallowed the words and gazed at Cheon Taemin, his eyes dark.

[P117]
He’d been right.

[P118]
He still had no definite proof or testimony, but Choi Minwoo’s words had made him see it again: Cheon Taemin and the Martial God had been the same person all along.

[P119]
The shadow of that old hero, sleeping as if dead, stretched across two worlds.

[P120]
*He knew it wasn’t over. He knew Asmodeus hadn’t been completely destroyed.*

[P121]
There was still so much Jin Taekyung hadn’t uncovered, so much he wanted to ask.

[P122]
But this was enough.

[P123]
At least he now knew what choice he had to make.

[P124]
Step.

[P125]
He turned without hesitation and started walking.

[P126]
He’d taken only a few steps when he noticed a tiny but important change and stopped.

[P127]
The door.

[P128]
It was gone.

[P129]
The only exit from this secret space, created through advanced magic, had vanished without a trace.

[P130]
“Team Leader.”

[P131]
At his quiet call, Jin Taekyung turned. Choi Minwoo stood there, his expression unwavering.

[P132]
“I’m sorry.”

[P133]
The brief, calm apology told Jin Taekyung everything.

[P134]
“Was this your plan from the beginning?”

[P135]
“As I said, we know what kind of person you are, Mr. Jin.”

[P136]
“We?”

[P137]
“Of course, I didn’t make this decision alone. Most of the others, including Mr. Johnson, have already agreed to the plan.”

[P138]
“Most? Then someone must have opposed this ridiculous plan.”

[P139]
“No. We didn’t tell anyone who might cause trouble. We couldn’t risk an unexpected complication. We’ve made every other preparation we could, too.”

[P140]
Thinking of Chuck Hagel and the Skeleton King, who still knew nothing about it, Choi Minwoo continued in a composed voice.

[P141]
“So… you’ll stay here with me for the time we have left, Mr. Jin.”

[P142]
The many people involved in the plan had a single goal: use every means at their disposal to keep Jin Taekyung—their only hope—here until the three days Morgoth had declared to the world were over.

[P143]
Fortunately, the secret chamber Jin Taekyung had chosen was perfectly suited to the plan. Countless barrier spells had been installed to protect Cheon Taemin.

[P144]
Even so, one unpredictable element remained: Jin Taekyung himself.

[P145]
The savior of a new age.

[P146]
The greatest and strongest Hunter in the world, successor to Cheon Taemin—a man no one else could replace.

[P147]
That was precisely why they couldn’t let him sacrifice himself in vain. And Choi Minwoo hadn’t forgotten one final precaution.

[P148]
“No matter how strong you are, Mr. Jin, you won’t be able to get out of here.”

[P149]
“Is that so?”

[P150]
Jin Taekyung reached into the air. A silver spear, invisible until now, appeared in his grasp.

[P151]
Whoosh.

[P152]
Dark blue flames surged along White Flame’s spearhead. The fire was refined to an extraordinary degree and carried heat beyond anything Choi Minwoo had felt from it the last time he’d seen it.

[P153]
But Choi Minwoo didn’t waver.

[P154]
“Come to think of it, there’s one thing I haven’t told you.”

[P155]
The final precaution he’d taken was never meant to counter Jin Taekyung’s strength.

[P156]
“If you try to break the barrier spells by force, the resulting backlash could bring down the entire Pentagon.”

[P157]
At least, Choi Minwoo didn’t waver until he heard Jin Taekyung’s answer.

[P158]
“You really think so?”

[P159]
Grgrgrk.

[P160]
The space around them warped in the terrible heat, and Jin Taekyung’s quiet voice echoed through it.

[P161]
“I think otherwise.”

[P162]
“…!”

[P163]
Choi Minwoo’s eyes widened.

[P164]
Slice.

Along a seam only one person could see, the vast wave of mana that joined and sustained hundreds of spells split in two.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
